title: The Confidence Code: The Science and Art of Self-Assurance – What Women Should Know
author: Katty Kay and Claire Shipman
target_audience: Women seeking to understand and build self-confidence
Professionals and leaders interested in women’s advancement
Organizations focused on diversity and gender equality
Readers of psychology and personal development
Individuals interested in the scientific and social aspects of confidence
core_themes: Understanding the sources and nature of confidence
The gap in confidence between men and women
Impact of confidence on success and leadership
Ways to develop and strengthen personal confidence
The intersection of genetics, upbringing, and societal influences on self-assurance
primary_purpose: To uncover what confidence actually is, why women often experience a confidence gap, and how both science and practical strategies can help women build lasting self-assurance in all areas of life.

structure_format.narrative_style: Blends investigative journalism, scientific research, personal anecdotes, and expert interviews
structure_format.organization: Structured into chapters exploring the definition, roots, obstacles, and practical strategies for building confidence, including real-life stories and actionable advice
features: Real-life interviews with women in various fields
Summaries of psychological and neurological research

key_concepts_lessons: Confidence is a combination of genetics, upbringing, environment, and practice.
Women, on average, tend to underestimate their abilities compared to men, often leading to missed opportunities.
Perfectionism and fear of failure can undermine confidence.
Action, risk-taking, and embracing imperfection are key habits of confident women.
Confidence can be cultivated deliberately, and small behavioral changes lead to greater self-assurance.
Societal expectations and workplace cultures can challenge or support the growth of women’s confidence.
notable_features: Focus on women and the unique challenges they face regarding confidence
Blend of scientific research and practical advice
Accessible writing style with actionable takeaways
Inclusion of stories from accomplished women leaders and high-achievers
cultural_historical_context: Published during ongoing global conversations about women’s empowerment, gender equity, and leadership, the book synthesizes research and real-world stories at a time when women’s confidence and advancement were being more directly addressed in public and corporate discourse.
reception_impact: National bestseller with strong media attention
Credited with starting important conversations around the confidence gap for women
Praised for making neuroscience and psychology accessible
Used as a resource in professional development and women’s leadership programs
Some critics note the initial focus is U.S.-centric and that men may also benefit from the insights
comparable_titles: Lean In: Women, Work, and the Will to Lead by Sheryl Sandberg
Presence: Bringing Your Boldest Self to Your Biggest Challenges by Amy Cuddy
Playing Big: Practical Wisdom for Women Who Want to Speak Up, Create, and Lead by Tara Mohr
